correctness.rationale: Vanishing of a coefficient vector on the full vertical line is equivalent, by the \(p\)-point Fourier transform, to zero left-vertex edge sums; vanishing on the diagonal similarly gives zero right-vertex sums; the extra point adds the weighted functional \(\psi_B\). Thus the kernel is exactly the unsigned incidence kernel intersected with one hyperplane. The incidence rank of a bipartite graph is \(n_B-c_B\), giving \(\beta_B=2p-n_B+c_B\) and the stated nullity drop by at most one. Invertibility forces \(\beta_B=1\), hence a spanning connected graph with \(2p\) vertices and edges, i.e. unicyclic. Its incidence kernel alternates on the unique even cycle, so the extra functional is \(S_C\). For prime \(p\), if the alternating label polynomial of degree at most \(p-1\) vanishes at a primitive \(p\)th root and at \(1\), cyclotomic divisibility forces all label-count differences to vanish, proving the multiset criterion. The reduced-incidence Laplace expansion yields the determinant after the two inverse Fourier row transforms. Independently, exhaustive \(p=3\) enumeration of all \(\binom96=84\) candidates found 75 invertible matrices and exactly the same 75 graph-criterion candidates, with zero mismatches.
correctness.risk: The determinant formula controls a product of singular values and does not determine the Riesz ratio asymptotics posed in the source.

final_claim: For the two-line-plus-one-point set \(E_p\subset\mathbb F_p^2\) of Ferguson--Mayeli--Sothanaphan, a \(2p\)-frequency set \(B\) is an exponential basis partner exactly when its associated bipartite graph on the \(b\)- and \(a+b\)-coordinates is spanning, connected and unicyclic and the two alternating matchings on its unique cycle have different label multisets. In that case \(|\det T(E_p,B)|=p^p|S_C|\), with \(S_C\) the alternating cyclotomic label sum; the submitted nullity formula holds for arbitrary \(B\) of size \(2p\).
limitations: The result does not determine \(\rho(E_p)\) or the smallest singular value over the surviving graphs.
The \(p=3\) exhaustive check is corroborative only.
